To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the enzymes involved in indole biosynthesis in Catharathus roseus have been isolated and purified and characterized biochemi­cally, and that the genes encoding the key enzymes have been isolated, characterized and functionally analyzed.

(1) the enzymes involved in indole and terpenoid biosynthesis are compartmentalized in different cell organelles and (2) the expression of genes involved in indode alkaloid biosynthesis are regulated by the plant hormones, jasmonates and salicylates.
the genes of tryptophan decarboxylase, geraniol 10-hydroxylase and strictosidine synthase are coordinately regulated by the jasmonate signal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes encoding the enzymes of the indole alkaloid pathway, and the elucidation of the mechanisms that control the expression and activity of the corresponding genes.
understanding the biosynthesis and regulation of the monomeric indol alkaloids in C. roseus.
the identification of enzymes and genes of indole alkaloids biosynthesis in Cathranthus roseus, and their regulation by endogenous and exogenous factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the indole alkaloid pathway is a highly regulated pathway.
the enzymes and genes of the indole alkaloid pathway have not been isolated in sufficient number to allow the construction of a detailed pathway.
the enzymes and genes involved and their regulation are not well understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the enzymes of indole alkaloids biosynthesis are not only present in the cytosol but also in the plastid, and the enzymes involved in the formation of monomeric alkaloids have been cloned.
we have been able to clone, express, purify and characterize a number of enzymes involved in the biosynthesis of the monomeric indoles, vindoline and cathranthine and also in the coupling reaction.
the enzymes of indole alkaloids biosynthesis are not only present in Catharanthus but also in some other species of Apocynaceae.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the biosynthesis of monomeric and dimeric indole alkaloids is a complex process that requires the concerted action of many enzymes and that their expression is tightly regulated at the transcription level.
the enzymes involved in indole and terpenoid pathways are regulated at different levels, i.e. transcription, translation and post-translationally.

the biosynthesis of indole alkaloids in C. roseus is a complex process involving many enzymes and that the enzymes and genes are regulated by many factors, including light, circadian rhythm and plant development.
